name: bash
description: The same shell as Bash. Call Bash.

name: monitor
description: Run a shell command as a background job and return its handle at once. Nothing arrives while it runs; when it exits, a notice says how it ended and points to its output file. Use a command that exits when the condition holds, for example `until grep -q READY app.log; do sleep 1; done`. timeout_ms stops it; without one it runs until stopped.

description.description: A few words naming what it waits for; the notice repeats them.

name: kill
description: The same job stop as TaskStop. Call TaskStop.

name: terminal
description: Run a program under a real terminal (40 rows by 120 columns), or drive a job this session started. With command, start the program and return its screen. With job, first type one of text, key, or secret_file (a host-side UTF-8 file); the record holds only the path, never the file's secret bytes. Then wait for pattern on the screen, quiet_ms without a screen change, the program's end, or timeout_ms (default 10000). With job alone, return the current screen immediately. A job id is job-N or its number. A job started by Bash can also be waited on here, using its plain output. Results give a status line (job id, running or how it ended, and the zero-based terminal cursor), followed by the screen rows or plain output; long output names its whole file.
